extracted.intended_audience: DoD acquisition officials, A-76 study teams, Working Capital Fund managers, policymakers and auditors involved in competitive sourcing
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for conducting an OMB Circular A-76 competitive sourcing study (the 12-step cost-comparison process) and for assessing whether A-76 is appropriate for revenue-generating functions in Defense Working Capital Fund activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objectives of the A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Three fundamental principles define the goals of the A-76 process: achieve economy and enhance productivity; keep inherently governmental functions “in-house”; and rely on the commercial sector for products and services if determined economical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A-76 to introduce competition to obtain cost savings and improved performance; ensure inherently governmental functions are excluded; balance cost savings with mission needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of competitive markets (appropriateness test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-76 assumes competitive markets with many competing suppliers capable of bidding; if competitive markets do not exist, OMB should reevaluate the use of the A-76 study to prevent non-value-added costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before initiating A-76, assess market presence and supplier capacity; if market competition is absent or limited, consider alternative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 applicability regardless of Command funding mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-76 process is indiscriminate to the type of Command being evaluated (Mission-Funded, Reimbursable, or Working Capital Fund); nowhere in OMB A-76 guidance is funding mechanism specified as a determinant of applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize A-76 applies broadly unless the function is specifically excluded by OMB; but the thesis examines whether application to DWCF revenue-generating (fee-for-service) activities is appropriate in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 Twelve-Step Process (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The A-76 is a comprehensive 12-step process that determines which functions will be retained by government workforce or contracted to commercial firms; it typically takes 18–36 months depending on complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan schedule/resources for an 18–36 month effort (streamlined variants exist); ensure all 12 steps are executed: Packaging; Public Announcement; PWS & QASP; Solicitation; Government Management Plan; Independent Review; Negotiation; Selection; Cost Comparison; Appeals; Implementation; Post-A-76 actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging (business unit definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Packaging (business unit definition) decides which commercial activities comprise the cost comparison and structures them into business units suitable for competition; effective packaging maximizes presence of competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bundle similar functions to create attractive bids; separate independent functions to avoid unrealistic multifunction contract demands; consider asset specificity, complexity and frequency when packaging to maximize contractor interest and fair competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public announcement and study team governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Public announcement notifies Congress, the local community and federal workforce that a commercial activity is under A-76 competition; the Unit Commander appoints a study team leader and designated team to oversee the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely notifications and designate a central point of contact and an experienced study team; complex operations may require outside consultants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation of Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS outlines product requirements, timeframes, performance measures and standards (forming the basis of the RFP). The QASP describes procedures to verify the selected proposal meets the PWS requirements, focusing on quality of products rather than provider procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest substantial effort in PWS development (cornerstone of the study). QASP should specify inspection methods, required reports, resources, and metrics/performance measures used for cost comparisons and contract oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and RFP requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation includes determining contract type, source selection plan, evaluation criteria, independent cost estimate and releasing the RFP. The RFP must specify that final award be solely on cost comparisons with in-house providers and include a 'First Refusal of Employment' clause for affected federal employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop evaluation criteria and ICE carefully; ensure RFP language enforces comparability and the first-refusal clause. If no private bids are received, the government retains the function but still must implement the MEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of Government Management Plan (MEO, IHCE, TPP, TP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Plan identifies the Government’s Most Efficient Organization (MEO) and serves as the basis for the In-House Cost Estimate (IHCE). The Plan comprises MEO, IHCE, Technical Performance Plan (TPP), and Transition Plan (TP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEO must specify organizational structure, staffing, operating procedures; IHCE must list overhead, staffing, severance, asset usage and all costs; TPP details how the government will meet PWS requirements; TP outlines transition to MEO or contractor. Errors in MEO yield incorrect IHCEs—careful construction is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Review (IRO)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Independent Review Officer, not involved in plan development, evaluates PWS, QASP, MEO, IHCE, TPP, and TP to ensure requirements are adequate and realistic and that costs and resource assumptions are justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select impartial IROs; the IRO must verify government capability and cost justification; independent review is critical to ensure a fair and defensible comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiation phase and selection of single provider
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer conducts discussions with private offerors (written/oral in accordance with FAR) to resolve proposal discrepancies. From proposals and any negotiated changes, the CO selects a single firm based on ability to meet MEO requirements; selection may be 'best value' prior to cost-comparison stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct FAR-compliant discussions to clarify proposals; be aware selection can be influenced by best-value decisions; document rationale for selection and equivalence to MEO scope for later cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison and minimum cost differential requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Source Selection Authority compares the in-house MEO/IHCE and the selected private sector proposal to determine equal level of performance; a contractor proposal must be at least 10% lower than the Government proposal or $10M less over the performance period (whichever is less) to pass the threshold for outsourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scope and performance equivalence before comparing costs; apply the minimum cost differential to account for conversion costs; if the contractor does not meet the threshold, the function remains government-run.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals focus on errors in the cost comparison steps and must be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer within the review period; appellants must have submitted a proposal (contractors), and federal employees or affected agencies may also appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain comprehensive documentation of cost comparison decisions and calculations; anticipate appeals and preserve auditable trails for contested items (cost inputs, scope definitions, IHCE adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of MEO or contractor organization and Post-MEO review
rubrics_metrics.description: Following final selection and appeals, the Transition Plan is executed addressing personnel management, transfer of equipment and procedural changes. If MEO is implemented, a formal Post-MEO Performance Review occurs after the first full year to confirm implementation per the Transition Plan and that actual costs align with IHCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execute transition per TP; schedule and conduct Post-MEO Performance Review to validate assumed efficiencies and cost estimates; use QASP during performance period regardless of outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post A-76 actions and QASP maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: After completion, the organization implements the QASP and periodically reviews it to ensure validity of the PWS. If MEO implemented, formal inspection and performance review verify MEO conformance and cost performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ongoing oversight metrics, update QASP as needed, and use periodic reviews to detect deviations from predicted performance or costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement of A-76 results — focus on personnel (FTE) savings
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 results historically show savings measured primarily via reduction in Civil Service Full Time Equivalent (FTE) employees; the thesis notes lack of documentation of operational (non-labor) savings and cautions that reported savings may primarily reflect personnel reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting A-76 savings, separate labor/FTE effects from non-labor operational savings; seek evidence of enduring operational efficiencies beyond personnel reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental Functions — exclusion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain functions deemed 'inherently governmental' must be excluded from A-76 competition (Appendix A illustrative list includes criminal investigations, command of military forces, foreign relations, agency policy determination, budget priorities, direction/control of employees, contract award/administration decisions, control of public funds, licensing/inspections, and adjudicatory hearings, among others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and exclude inherently governmental tasks during Packaging and baseline inventory (FAIR Act inventory); consult OFPP guidance and Appendix A examples when defining scope for competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations specific to Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF) activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Because DWCF activities (fee-for-service organizations) already compete for business and price outputs to recover costs, the thesis hypothesizes that many DWCF revenue-generating functions have already realized market efficiencies, making full A-76 studies potentially inappropriate or redundant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the DWCF activity is 'pre-competed' and already operating under market pressures; evaluate alternative cost-cutting or oversight processes tailored to DWCF (e.g., functional assessments) rather than full A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges and impediments specific to applying A-76 at WCF organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges include DWCF uniqueness relative to free market, pre-existing competition, civil service employment rules that hinder workforce adjustments, asset specificity, and the long duration between baseline inventory and study completion (3–4 years) allowing routine management changes to be misattributed to A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and weigh these constraints when deciding to proceed; consider shorter, current-evidence assessments to avoid conflating incidental management savings with A-76 outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended alternative: 'Functional Assessment with teeth' (simplified cost-comparison snapshot)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended alternative is a Functional Assessment augmented by a simplified external cost-comparison (a 'snapshot') that evaluates WCF work done in last 6 months against outside vendors; if WCF cost is 10% higher than market, proceed to a full study. The entire process should be completed in a maximum of 9 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the snapshot to limit cost and time exposure; apply the 10% threshold to trigger full A-76 only when potential savings justify full study; document methodology, vendors used for market comparisons, and timeline (target 9 months).
